narrativeBlocks.title: The undying abductor
narrativeBlocks.body: Koschei the Deathless is the Slavic cycle's great villain — a withered sorcerer who abducts brides and heroes' loves and cannot be killed, because his death is not in him.

narrativeBlocks.title: A nesting doll of death
narrativeBlocks.body: His death is hidden inside layers: on the tip of a needle, inside an egg, inside a duck, inside a hare, inside an iron chest, buried under an oak on the island of Buyan at the edge of the world.

narrativeBlocks.title: Only helpers reach it
narrativeBlocks.body: No hero fights Koschei head-on and wins. The path to the egg runs through helpers — a wolf, an eagle, a pike — each earned by a kindness the hero did earlier. The chain of favours is the actual weapon.

narrativeBlocks.title: The egg in his face
narrativeBlocks.body: When the egg is finally brought to Koschei, the hero doesn't even need to break it: holding it, he can make the sorcerer helpless — crushing it kills him. The most dangerous thing in the world is his own hidden death.

narrativeBlocks.title: Death externalized
narrativeBlocks.body: The pattern — a giant whose life is hidden outside his body — is one of folklore's most travelled ideas (the giant's heart in the well, the troll's heart in the egg). It says: the unkillable are still fragile — you just have to find where the fragility lives.

quiz.prompt: Where does Koschei keep his death?

choices.text: In a ring on his finger
In the roots of the world-tree
On a needle's tip, in an egg, in a duck, in a hare, in a chest under an oak on the island of Buyan
In a stone in his chest

quiz.explanation: The nested hiding — needle, egg, duck, hare, chest, island — is the tale's famous riddle.

quiz.prompt: How does the hero finally defeat Koschei?

choices.text: He gains the egg through helpers earned by earlier kindnesses — holding or crushing it ends the sorcerer
He burns the iron chest on a pyre
He beheads Koschei in single combat

quiz.explanation: The weapon is the favours-chain — kindnesses, not swords, reach the death.
